summary: All round-1 findings addressed correctly. CR8-001 is resolved: the one-level nesting assumption is now documented in the step comment, and the post-normalization grep guard catches layout regressions at release time rather than at first install. CR8-002 was explicitly left as-is per guidance. One informational observation on empty-SHA256SUMS edge case — not actionable. No new issues introduced. The diff is clean.

findings.title: No guard for empty SHA256SUMS (zero build artifacts case)
findings.description: The normalization guard (`if grep -q '/' SHA256SUMS; then exit 1; fi`) catches leftover path separators after sed. It does NOT catch the case where `find` matches zero tarballs and SHA256SUMS is empty. An empty SHA256SUMS would still be uploaded to the GitHub Release, and the shim's install-binary.ts would fail with 'SHA256SUMS does not include an entry for <filename>' — a user-visible error rather than a silent corruption.
findings.impact: This scenario requires the build-linux and build-macos jobs to have both produced no artifacts, which would mean both matrix legs failed. In that case, the `needs: [build-linux, build-macos]` would also fail and the release job would not run. So an empty SHA256SUMS from zero artifacts is structurally impossible given the current workflow DAG — both build jobs must succeed (and produce tarballs) for the release job to trigger.
findings.recommendation: Not actionable — the failure mode is structurally impossible given `needs: [build-linux, build-macos]`. Documenting for completeness.

CR8-001.description: The step comment now explicitly documents the one-level-deep artifact layout assumption (upload-artifact names by target triple, download-artifact materializes exactly one subdirectory per artifact). The post-normalization `grep -q '/'` guard correctly fires if any line still contains a slash after sed — this catches both deeper nesting and a completely failed normalization. Logic verified: valid tarball names (mnemonic-mcp-${tag}-${target}.tar.gz) contain no slashes, so the guard does not produce false positives. A simulated nested-path scenario would leave '/' in the filename portion and trigger exit 1.

CR8-002.description: Leave-as-is per round-1 guidance. The prepublishOnly double-build is intentional belt-and-suspenders.

concurrency_block.analysis: Workflow-level concurrency keyed on `github.ref` with `cancel-in-progress: true` is the standard pattern for tag-triggered release workflows. Correctly prevents race conditions on GitHub Release asset uploads and Trusted-Publishing OIDC token reuse when a tag is force-pushed. The cancel applies to all jobs including publish-npm and publish-mcp-shim — acceptable tradeoff since tag re-pushes are typically corrective actions where abandoning the in-flight run is intentional. One nuance: if the release job is mid-execution (partially uploaded artifacts) and is cancelled, GitHub Release state may be partial. This is the standard accepted risk of cancel-in-progress on release workflows and is preferable to double-publishing.

sha256sums_comment_expansion.analysis: The expanded comment accurately documents the layout contract (upload-artifact@v4 names by target triple, download-artifact@v4 materializes one subdir per artifact). The cross-reference to SAR8-M1 and CR8-001 makes the audit trail clear. No inaccuracies.

post_normalization_guard.analysis: `grep -q '/'` on the post-sed SHA256SUMS exits 0 only if a slash is present, which triggers the explicit `exit 1` with a clear error message on stderr. Correct inversion logic. Edge case: empty SHA256SUMS passes the guard silently but is structurally impossible (see CR8-R2-INFO1 above). The error message includes `cat SHA256SUMS >&2` for immediate debugging visibility — good practice.

attest_comment_update.analysis: The updated comment accurately explains why the subject-path covers only the tarball (not the extracted binary): `gh attestation verify` runs against the tarball before extraction in install-binary.ts, and the tarball digest already commits to its contents. The cross-reference to Decision 8 and SAR8-M2 is accurate.

publish_mcp_shim_comment_update.analysis: The expanded header comment explains the deliberate absence of `needs: [publish-npm]` and provides a forward-looking maintenance note: if a future change adds a workspace dep on sdk/cli, the `needs:` must be extended to avoid shipping a shim referencing an unpublished SDK/CLI version. This is the right pattern for documenting intentional architectural constraints.

ac_verification.note: The round-2 changes are additive (concurrency block, comment expansions, post-normalization guard). None of the changes remove or alter existing functionality. All 9 task ACs verified in round 1 continue to pass.
